evidence: app/package.json:9 — next 16.4.3, the current active-LTS stable (confirmed via nextjs.org October 2026 release notes and security post)
app/next.config.ts:1-10 — only long-stable config flags (poweredByHeader, compress) plus top-level turbopack.root, a stable documented option
app/lib/api.ts:20 — plain fetch with cache:'no-store' plus a hand-rolled in-memory TTL cache; no 'use cache' or Cache Components
app/app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:18,33 — awaited Promise params/searchParams, the standard stable Next 15+ pattern
app/components/Filters.tsx:3 — usePathname/useRouter and basic React hooks only
reach.rationale: Zero experimental, preview, RC or canary APIs; the newest thing in the app is the Next 16.4.3 dependency itself, which is the current stable LTS release, and every API consumed from it is long-stable.

evidence: app/next.config.ts:9 — the only forward-looking knob (turbopack.root) is a single isolated config entry, trivially removable
app/lib/api.ts:1-44 — all framework-adjacent behavior (fetch semantics, caching) is centralized in one thin module, so any future migration to Cache Components touches one file
containment.rationale: There is nothing experimental to contain; the one borderline-new setting is a one-line config entry and all data fetching lives behind a single module boundary.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:18-30 — request-time fetch with short in-memory TTL, exactly what SPEC.md requires (live data, runtime caching allowed) — no experimental API needed
app/next.config.ts:7 — compress:false justified by the spec's reverse-proxy instruction
justification.rationale: No experimental API is used, and the conservative choices are each traceable to spec requirements (live request-time data, proxy-handled compression), so nothing was adopted for novelty.

findings.issue: The app hand-rolls an in-memory promise/TTL cache instead of Next 16.4's Cache Components ('use cache'), which Vercel now recommends for every app and which becomes the default model in Next 17.
findings.suggestion: Not a defect for this dimension — the current approach is stable and spec-compliant — but budget a future migration to the Cache Components model when upgrading to Next 17.

summary: This is a maximally conservative codebase: current stable Next (16.4.3, active LTS) with exclusively long-stable App Router APIs and zero experimental/preview/canary surface. The only forward-looking item is the one-line stable turbopack.root config. Risk of breaking changes from upstream experiments is essentially nil; the only latent cost is that it hasn't adopted the Cache Components model Vercel now recommends, which is a migration consideration rather than a current problem.
